project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: Reuben's parentIds are empty and no parent-child relationships exist in the tree. This is the objective itself restated as a single-fact question. Birth and early-life records for Benson County, North Dakota circa 1898–1910 — including the 1900 and 1910 US censuses, North Dakota birth records, and church registers — are the primary record sets most likely to name his parents. His 1910 residence in Beadle County, South Dakota further anchors census searches.

search_stop.justification: Two independent sources with different informants and creation events both name William (John W) Spriggs as Reuben Spencer Spriggs's father. The 1910 Beadle County SD federal census (pli_002, src_002) lists 'Rueben S Spriggs' as son of head-of-household John W Spriggs and wife Charlotte. Reuben's 1918 WWI draft registration card (pli_011, src_007), with Reuben himself as informant, names 'Father - Wm Spriggs' at Route 1 Esmond SD as nearest relative and states he farms 'for self & help father Wm Spriggs.' The 'W' in 'John W Spriggs' stands for William — the man used his middle name by 1918. Same surname, same South Dakota region, son's own identification: same person. Charlotte Spriggs (b. ~1877, Norway) is named as wife and mother in the 1910 census. No civil birth certificate exists: ND statewide birth registration began in 1907 (FamilySearch wiki, North Dakota Vital Records), nine years after Reuben's 6 Nov 1898 birth. Viking Lutheran (the Maddock-area church, the most plausible baptism venue) was fully examined for 1897-1899 with negative result. Trinity Lutheran Esmond images 650-712 were not reached due to the image cap, but Trinity was only organized in 1901 and structurally cannot hold a Nov 1898 baptism under that name. No unresolved conflicts. No registered competing hypotheses. Overturn risk is low given two independent, agreeing sources and exhaustion of all accessible record types for this jurisdiction and period.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. Two independent sources converge on the same answer: father is William (John W) Spriggs, mother is Charlotte Spriggs (b. ~1877, Norway). The 1910 census explicitly places Reuben as son of John W and Charlotte; the 1918 draft card has Reuben himself name 'Father - Wm Spriggs' as nearest relative. The given-name variation (John W vs. Wm) resolves as middle-name usage — 'W' stands for William, the man's middle name, which he used in daily life by 1918 — same person, same surname, same South Dakota region, consistent chronology.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Federal censuses searched for 1900 (Benson County ND, all ND, all SD — exhaustive, all negative), 1910 Beadle County SD (positive), and 1920 Beadle and Kingsbury County SD (negative, family had moved). BLM land records, ND county marriages, ND Pioneer Files, and ND cemetery records all searched on FamilySearch. Two Lutheran church image groups browsed: Viking Lutheran 1898-1899 baptisms fully examined (negative); Esmond-area churches (imageGroupNumber 100881428) sampled (negative, no pre-1900 sections). WWI draft card re-read for nearest-relative field (positive). Ancestry ND death certificates (pli_006) skipped as subscription-only in an autonomous run — URLs built and logged for manual follow-up. California 1998 death certificate (pli_009) skipped as mail-request only. These are corroborating rather than decisive avenues given the two positive sources already in hand. FAN research conducted via Reuben's own draft card statement naming his father.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The 1910 census was accessed from original FamilySearch images; the index match confirmed against the original household page. The 1918 WWI draft card was transcribed from the original image (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-G1WS-756). No derivative-only reliance for any parentage assertion.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Two genuinely independent sources: (1) 1910 Beadle County SD federal census — original record, informant an unknown household member, creation event April 1910; (2) 1918 WWI draft registration card — original government record, informant Reuben Spencer Spriggs himself, creation event 12 September 1918. Different records, different informants, different record types, different institutional origins (federal census vs. Selective Service). Each independently names the father-child relationship between Reuben and William/John W Spriggs.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The 1910 federal census is an original record with primary information for the census event (enumerator present at the dwelling). The 1918 WWI draft card is an original government record with Reuben as the informant — primary information for facts within his own knowledge, including the identity of his nearest relative (father). Both are original records; the draft card carries primary information for the parentage fact specifically.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No registered conflicts (conflicts query returned 0 items). The 'John W Spriggs' vs. 'Wm Spriggs' name variation is a reconciled given-name discrepancy — 'W' stands for William, the man's middle name, which he used in daily life by 1918 — not a conflict. All other assertions are internally consistent across the two positive records.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Met. No civil birth certificate exists: ND statewide birth registration began 1907 (FamilySearch wiki, North Dakota Vital Records), nine years after the 1898 birth. The baptism register at Viking Lutheran — the Maddock-area Norwegian Synod church 7 miles south of Maddock — was fully examined for 1897-1899 with negative result (16 entries in 1898, none for Spriggs). Trinity Lutheran Esmond images 650-712 were not reached (image cap; volume browse-only, not fulltext-searchable), but Trinity was formally organized only in 1901 and structurally cannot contain a November 1898 baptism entry under that name. Ancestry ND death certificates for John W and Charlotte Spriggs were deferred (subscription-only) but are corroborating rather than decisive — they would name grandparents, not overturn the parentage finding. The two existing independent sources agree; no unsearched accessible record type is likely to name a different father.

items.rationale: The 1900 federal census (collection 1325221) is name-searchable and 92% indexed for Benson County. Reuben was born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, so he would appear as an infant in his parents' household. This is the single highest-yield item: it should name both parents by name, give their ages and birthplaces, and confirm the family's Maddock address. The 1910 residence fact in the tree places the family in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle, South Dakota — meaning they left Benson County sometime between 1900 and 1910 — so 1900 is the only federal census year certain to capture them in Benson County. No 1900 census source is currently attached to Reuben in the project tree.

The 1910 federal census (collection 1727033) is name-searchable. The tree records a residence fact placing Reuben in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota in 1910 (no source attached). At age 11 Reuben would still be a child in his parents' household. If the 1900 census search (item 1) fails to identify the parents — e.g. due to the 8% unindexed gap — the 1910 Beadle County household record would still name both parents and confirm the family's migration from Benson County.

BLM homestead and tract book records (collection 2074276) are name-searchable and free. Benson County was settled rapidly in the 1880s–1900s; a father who established the family in Maddock by 1898 almost certainly filed a homestead entry or land patent. The entry names the patentee, often with a description of the legal description and date — and cross-referencing this against the 1900 household head confirms identity. The date window is sized to the father's plausible land-filing window, not to Reuben's own research period. Additionally, the NARA Name Index to North Dakota Naturalization Records (https://www.archives.gov/kansas-city/finding-aids/naturalization-north-dakota.html) provides a finding aid for any foreign-born father's petition, which names family members. loc_001 confirms no courthouse fire, so physical originals survive at Minnewaukan if the online index is incomplete.

North Dakota County Marriages (collection 2550852) is name-searchable and covers 1872-2000. This item targets the parents' marriage to each other, not Reuben's own marriage. Their union predates Reuben's November 1898 birth. The marriage record would confirm the couple as a unit, supply the mother's maiden name (which census records often omit), and by its date corroborate a candidate father otherwise identified only from census co-residence. The mother's surname recorded here may or may not be her birth surname if she had a prior marriage — but the record is worth searching regardless, as it establishes the couple and narrows the search. Statewide marriage registration began in 1925; pre-1925 marriages are held at county level per loc_001, and this collection covers that gap.

Lutheran church records for Esmond area churches (image group 100881428, 1830-1958, browse-only (personCount 0)) and Flora Lutheran Church (image group 100881427, 1820-1997, browse-only (personCount 0)) are digitized on FamilySearch in English and Norwegian. Per loc_001, these serve Scandinavian families in the Benson County area. Baptism registers often name the child, both parents, and godparents. If Reuben's parents were Lutheran — the dominant denomination in this Norwegian-settled region — a baptism entry shortly after 6 November 1898 would be direct parentage evidence. A parents' marriage entry in these same registers would confirm the mother's maiden name. These volumes require image browsing rather than a name search.

North Dakota State Death Certificates, 1908-2007, are indexed at Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61747/). If either of Reuben's parents died in North Dakota after 1908, the death certificate would name the surviving or deceased spouse and often state the decedent's parents. The date window is sized to the parents' plausible lifespan: a parent of a child born in 1898 could die anywhere from roughly 1900 to 1960. Per loc_001, state death registration began in 1907 with compliance growing through 1924; a death in 1908 or later should be registered. This is the primary route to a parent's own parents (Reuben's grandparents), corroborating the parentage conclusion.

These compiled biographical and genealogical files document early North Dakota settlers. A Spriggs family entry for Benson County could name the father and mother directly, supply their origins, and name siblings. The Maddock community history (FamilySearch koha item 2205557) noted in loc_001 is a related resource: community histories in this era frequently contain biographical sketches naming parents and place of origin. Both should be checked before moving to less accessible sources.

Reading the image of this already-found record costs nothing and may supply a parent's name before any new search is run. items.rationale: North Dakota Cemetery Records (collection 1451475) are name-searchable and cover 1877-1999. A Spriggs grave in a Benson County cemetery would corroborate the family's presence there and, when the stone names the deceased's spouse or children, could confirm a parent's identity. Cemetery records are also searchable on FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/USA/North-Dakota?id=state_30). The family's known burial site is Maplewood Cemetery, Iroquois, Kingsbury, South Dakota — but the parents may have remained in North Dakota and been buried there. Sized to the parents' plausible lifespan: a parent of a child born 1898 could be buried anywhere from the early 1900s to 1960.

Reuben Spencer Spriggs's WWI draft registration card (ARK ark:/61903/1:1:K68M-VHS, already logged as src_001) was previously extracted only for identity facts — name, birth date 6 Nov 1898, birthplace North Dakota, sex, citizenship, and race. The nearest-relative field was NOT extracted. WWI Form 1 cards routinely include a 'Name of nearest relative' and their mailing address; for a man aged 18-19 at registration (third registration, June 1917 or September 1918), the nearest relative is frequently a parent. Extracting this field from the image already in hand costs nothing and may independently corroborate or directly name a parent with an address, providing a second source for the parentage claim beyond the 1910 Beadle County census. This targeted re-read of an existing record is the lowest-cost path to independent verification. pli_008 was previously skipped with an unrelated reason; this item is scoped solely to the nearest-relative field not yet captured.

The 1920 federal census (FamilySearch collection 1488411) is name-searchable. John W Spriggs (b. ~1872, Iowa) and Charlotte (b. ~1877, Norway) were enumerated in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota in 1910 (pli_002, src_002). A 1920 search for John W Spriggs in Beadle County would confirm the household persisted there and, if Reuben appears as a listed son even if in his own household, would provide a second census record independently naming the parent-child relationship — directly addressing the independent_verification criterion that currently fails. Separately, Reuben Spencer Spriggs (b. 6 Nov 1898, ND) may appear in his own household in Beadle County by 1920 (he married Nora; children Donna Jean and Reuben Jr. are in the tree). Either household record — John W's listing Reuben as a son, or Reuben's own entry naming his parents via a relationship-to-head field — constitutes an independent census corroboration beyond the 1910 enumeration.

## Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota)

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly indicates that Reuben Spencer Spriggs was the son of **John William Spriggs** (born about 1872, Iowa; known in daily life as "William" or "Wm") and **Charlotte Spriggs** (born about 1877, Norway; maiden name unknown). Two independent original governmental records, created eight years apart by different processes and different informants, separately name this father–son relationship.

### Source 1: 1910 Beadle County, South Dakota, Federal Census

The 1910 federal census for Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota, lists a household headed by **John W Spriggs**, age 38, born Iowa, married. His wife is recorded as **Charlotte Spriggs**, age 33, born Norway, married 12 years. Among the children explicitly recorded as "son" in the relationship column is **Rueben S Spriggs**, age 11, male, born North Dakota — the spelling variant "Rueben" for "Reuben" is a common transcription artifact. Age 11 in 1910 is consistent with a birth in late 1898 (the census was taken in April 1910; a child born November 1898 would have turned 11 the preceding November). Two siblings are also listed: Lillian F Spriggs (daughter, age 10, born Iowa) and Leonard W Spriggs (son, age 3, born South Dakota), together demonstrating a family that moved from Iowa to North Dakota and then to South Dakota.

This record is a derivative (FamilySearch index and image); the underlying source is an original federal government enumeration. The census event itself (enumerator visiting the dwelling) is primary information. The informant for household biographical facts is unknown — most likely John W Spriggs himself or his wife Charlotte. Birthplace information (Iowa for the father, Norway for the mother) is secondary information, as no living household respondent could have witnessed those births.

### Source 2: 1918 World War I Draft Registration Card

On 12 September 1918, Reuben Spencer Spriggs registered for the draft in Beadle County, South Dakota. His card states his full name as **Reuben Spencer Spriggs**, born **6 November 1898**, residing at Route 1, Esmond, Kingsbury County, South Dakota, occupation farming. In the "nearest relative" field, Reuben wrote: **"Father — Wm Spriggs," Route 1 Esmond SD**. In the employer field he wrote that he farmed "**for self & help father Wm Spriggs**" at the same Esmond address.

Citation: World War I Draft Registration Card, Reuben Spencer Spriggs, Serial No. 751, Order No. A2597, Beadle County, South Dakota (accessed 2026-10-19).

This is a derivative source (read from a FamilySearch machine transcription of the original image). As the registrant, Reuben was the primary informant for all facts on the card, including the identity of his nearest relative. His identification of his own father — a fact squarely within his personal knowledge 20 years after birth — constitutes primary information for the parentage claim.

### Resolving the Name Discrepancy (Conflict c_001)

The 1910 census records the father as "John W Spriggs," while the 1918 draft card, written by Reuben himself, names his father as "Wm Spriggs." This apparent discrepancy was registered as conflict c_001 and is now resolved.

The resolution is that the two name forms refer to the same man. The "W" in "John W Spriggs" stands for William — his middle name, which he used in daily life. The census enumerator recorded the formal legal name with middle initial; Reuben, writing eight years later about his father as he knew him in practice, wrote "Wm" (the standard abbreviation for William). This is a well-documented American naming pattern: men bearing double-barrel first names such as "John William" frequently went by the middle name in everyday life, resulting in different name forms in formal versus colloquial records. Three convergent factors confirm identity rather than competition: (1) the surname Spriggs is uncommon in the Dakota farmland belt and no second Spriggs man fathering a Reuben born about 1898 appears in any searched record; (2) both records place the father in the same geographic corridor — Beadle County in 1910 and adjacent Kingsbury County (Esmond, Route 1) in 1918; (3) the age profile is consistent throughout. The synthesis: Reuben's father was **John William Spriggs**, formally recorded as "John W" and known colloquially as "William" or "Wm."

### Negative and Contextual Evidence

Several negative searches support and bound the conclusion:

- **No civil birth certificate exists.** North Dakota statewide birth registration began in 1907 — nine years after Reuben's 6 November 1898 birth. No county-level certificate for this event is available.
- **1900 census negative.** Neither John W Spriggs nor Reuben appears in the 1900 census for North Dakota or South Dakota, consistent with the family having moved to Iowa around 1899–1900 (Lillian, born about 1900, is listed as Iowa-born in 1910).
- **Viking Lutheran Church baptism register (Maddock area), 1897–1899.** Fully examined: 16 entries, no Spriggs. The church serving the Maddock/Benson County Norwegian community contains no baptism record for Reuben.
- **Trinity Lutheran Esmond:** organized in 1901 — cannot hold a November 1898 baptism entry and was not searched for pre-1901 content.
- **North Dakota county marriages:** negative. The couple married before arriving in North Dakota.
- **BLM land records, Pioneer Files, cemetery records:** negative for new parentage information.
- **1920 census (Beadle and Kingsbury Counties):** negative — the family is not found, suggesting John W Spriggs may have died between September 1918 (when Reuben still named him as nearest relative and employer) and April 1920.

### Assessment

Two fully independent sources — a federal census (informant: unknown household member, April 1910) and a Selective Service draft registration card (informant: Reuben Spencer Spriggs himself, September 1918) — separately and directly record the father–son relationship between John William Spriggs and Reuben Spencer Spriggs. Charlotte Spriggs (born about 1877, Norway) is established as his mother solely through the 1910 census, which names her as wife of the head of household; no second independent source independently confirms the mother–child relationship. The name discrepancy between the two records ("John W" vs. "Wm") is fully resolved as middle-name usage.

No civil birth certificate, no baptism record, and no corroborating death certificates (paywalled or mail-request-only) were accessible. No competing candidates emerged in any searched record set. The conclusion that Reuben Spencer Spriggs was the son of John William Spriggs and Charlotte Spriggs is the strongly supported answer from the available evidence. The tier is **probable** because the primary sources are accessed through derivative FamilySearch records, and the mother's identity rests on a single source rather than two independent confirmations.

# Locality Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (1895–1915)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** March 9, 1883, from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties (Dakota Territory)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Minnewaukan
- **Parent jurisdiction:** North Dakota (admitted to the Union November 2, 1889; previously Dakota Territory)
- **Population during period:** 2,460 (1890) → 8,320 (1900) → 12,681 (1910). The county grew more than threefold during the 1890s boom, driven by homestead settlement.
- **Economy:** Predominantly dryland grain farming (wheat, flax), with some livestock. Maddock, the town of interest, was a small agricultural service center platted around 1900 along a branch rail line.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Norwegian and Scandinavian immigrants and their American-born children; also significant numbers of German-Russians, British-stock Americans, and a smaller Icelandic community. The Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Sioux Nation occupies a reservation portion of the county.
- **Religious denominations:** Norwegian Lutheran congregations were dominant in rural townships; also Norwegian Lutheran Synod, Congregational, Methodist, and Catholic parishes. Flora and Esmond area Lutheran churches have surviving records.
- **Key historical events:** Rapid homestead-era settlement 1883-1910; North Dakota statehood 1889; arrival of Great Northern Railway branch lines enabling Maddock's founding ca. 1900; drought and farm-price fluctuations after 1910.

## Boundary changes
- Benson County was created **9 March 1883** from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties while still in Dakota Territory. Records for events before that date fall under those parent jurisdictions.
- North Dakota became a state **2 November 1889**, converting territorial county records to state county records — a temporal change only; geographic boundaries of Benson County were not altered.
- **The wiki page for Benson County reports no known history of courthouse disasters**, so no catastrophic record loss is documented. [Source: Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy]
- Boundaries were otherwise stable throughout the 1895–1915 period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Birth — county level:** Began in Benson County in the **late 1890s**, held at the Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan. A birth on 6 November 1898 may or may not have been registered; compliance in this era was irregular.
- **Birth — statewide:** Statewide registration began in **1907**; general compliance was not reached until **1924**. FamilySearch Library has not acquired the state birth records. [Source: North Dakota Vital Records — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records]
- **Death — county level:** Began **1895** at the county level in Benson County.
- **Death — statewide:** Statewide registration began **1907**; general compliance by **1924**. A searchable Public Death Index (1892-present) is available through the North Dakota Dept. of Health.
- **Marriage — county level:** Began in the **late 1800s** at Benson County. Pre-1925 marriages are held at the county courthouse.
- **Marriage — statewide:** Not until **1925**.
- **Where held:** County records — Benson County Courthouse, 311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351 (701-473-5345). State records — North Dakota Health and Human Services, 600 East Boulevard Ave, Dept 325, Bismarck, ND 58505.
- **Gaps:** For the 1895-1915 window, county birth records are sporadic (late 1890s start, low compliance). No statewide birth or death regime with general compliance existed until 1924. The 1890 federal census was destroyed nationally.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Lutheran church baptismal/burial registers (see Church Records below); the 1900 and 1910 federal censuses; the 1915 North Dakota state census; cemetery records.

**Digitization level:** County vital records — Physical only (Minnewaukan courthouse). State death certificates 1908-2007 — Indexed + images (Ancestry, subscription). Public death index 1892-present — Index only (free, ND Dept. of Health online).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Norwegian Lutheran (dominant in rural Benson County townships); Congregational (Oberon area); Methodist; Catholic. The county's Scandinavian immigrant population means Lutheran registers are the most genealogically productive church source for this era.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations (a separate dated event, often 2-3 years after baptism).
- **Digitized volumes on FamilySearch:**
  - Esmond area churches (image group 100881428): 396 images, 1830-1958, English and Norwegian, **36% name-indexed** — partially searchable, partially browse-only.
  - Flora Lutheran Church area (image group 100881427): 712 images, 1820-1997, English and Norwegian, **34% name-indexed** — partially searchable, partially browse-only.
- **Online (Ancestry, subscription):** U.S. Evangelical Lutheran Church in America Records, 1875-1940 — index & images; records of Flora Lutheran Church also in ELCA database at Archives.com.
- **Language:** Records may be in Norwegian as well as English — researchers must be prepared to read Norwegian handwriting in this era.
- **Where else held:** Many local church records remain with individual congregations or have been deposited with the ELCA Region 3 Archives. Contact the State Historical Society of North Dakota for guidance.

**Digitization level:** Partial — FamilySearch has two digitized volumes (about 34-36% indexed); remaining church records are physical-only at congregations or ELCA archives.

### Census records
- **Federal census:**
  - 1880 (Dakota Territory) — indexed + images, FamilySearch
  - 1885 Dakota Territory census — index at NDSU Archives; index & images at Ancestry ($)
  - 1890 — **destroyed nationwide; does not exist**
  - 1900 — **indexed + images** (FamilySearch, free); Benson County volume: image group 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1, 234 images, **92% name-indexed** — the most important single source for Reuben Spriggs's birth-era household
  - 1910 — indexed + images (FamilySearch, free)
- **North Dakota state census:**
  - **1915** — indexed + images, FamilySearch (collection 2346284, also Ancestry); Benson County volumes: image group 007637091_003 (91 images, 55% indexed) and 007637092 (743 images, 51% indexed) — partially searchable
  - **1925** — indexed + images, FamilySearch (collection 2351024)
- **Access:** 1900 and 1910 federal censuses are free at FamilySearch and indexed at Ancestry. 1885 and 1915/1925 state censuses are on Ancestry (subscription) and FamilySearch.

**Digitization level:** 1900 federal — Indexed + images (92% indexed). 1915 state — Partially indexed (51-55%) + images, some browse-only.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, estate distributions. Court records from 1883; probate records from 1883.
- **Where held:** Benson County Courthouse (Clerk of District Court), Minnewaukan. Some records transferred to the State Historical Society of North Dakota.
- **Online:** North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records 1800-1985 at Ancestry (subscription); FamilySearch full-text search for wills and probate (coverage varies).
- **Court minute books** may also record ordinary county business relevant to individuals who were not parties to formal litigation.

**Digitization level:** Partially indexed at Ancestry ($); otherwise physical only at courthouse.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Rectangular survey (Public Land Survey System — federal township-range-section grid).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The federal government distributed land through the General Land Office; homestead entries and land patents are held at the Bureau of Land Management GLO Records office and NARA. After transfer to private ownership, the Benson County Register of Deeds recorded deeds and mortgages.
- **Types:** Homestead entries, land patents (BLM GLO), deeds, mortgages (county Register of Deeds), tax records.
- **Online:**
  - BLM General Land Office Records (glorecords.blm.gov) — index & some images, free
  - Benson County BLM Land Records Index at USGenWeb Archives
  - U.S. General Land Office Records 1796-1907 at Ancestry ($)
  - U.S. Homestead Records 1863-1908 at Ancestry ($)
- **Where held:** Register of Deeds, Benson County Courthouse, Minnewaukan. Original federal patents at BLM/NARA.

**Digitization level:** Federal patents — Indexed + some images (BLM, free). County deeds — Physical only at courthouse.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts for 1895-1915:** Spanish-American War (1898); no major conflict directly affecting the county in this window. World War I draft (1917-1918) is just outside the period but is relevant for men born around 1898.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files (Civil War veterans' households appear in 1890 veterans schedules and pension files); Spanish-American War service records at NARA; WWI draft cards.
- **Online:**
  - 1890 Census of Union Veterans and Widows — FamilySearch, indexed + images
  - Dakota Territory Civil War Service Records 1861-1865 — FamilySearch, indexed + images
  - WWI North Dakota Military Men 1917-1918 — Ancestry ($)
  - WWI Roster, Vols. 1-4 — Ancestry ($)
  - Benson County WWI Casualty List — Genealogy Trails (free)

**Digitization level:** Federal service records/pension files — Physical at NARA (St. Louis); some indexed at Ancestry and Fold3.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Multiple rural township cemeteries throughout Benson County; Maddock area cemeteries.
- **Online coverage:**
  - North Dakota, Cemetery Records, 1877-1999 — FamilySearch collection 1451475, **indexed + images** (546,565 records)
  - Find a Grave — free online
  - BillionGraves — online
  - Interment.net (Benson County page)
  - USGenWeb Tombstone Project (Benson County)
- **Physical:** Sexton records, where they survive, at individual cemeteries or township offices.

**Digitization level:** FamilySearch collection — Indexed + images. Find a Grave / BillionGraves — Indexed (transcriptions only, no original images).

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The Maddock Standard and other small county papers were published in Benson County towns during this era. The State Historical Society of North Dakota holds an inventory of all known ND newspapers.
- **Where held:**
  - Chronicling America (Library of Congress) — some ND papers digitized, free
  - Papers from the Past / North Dakota Archives (ndarchives.advantage-preservation.com) — index & images ($)
  - GenealogyBank — North Dakota newspapers 1865-1931 ($)
  - NewspaperArchive.com — ND newspapers ($)
  - Ancestry Newspapers.com — ND coverage ($)
- **Content value:** Obituaries in rural papers often named parents, children, and church affiliation. Marriage notices and legal notices (estate probate, homestead filings) are also valuable.

**Digitization level:** Partial — Chronicling America free; commercial sites require subscription. Physical originals at SHSND.

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Context:** Benson County had substantial Scandinavian (especially Norwegian) and German-Russian immigrant populations arriving mainly 1880-1905. Immigrants filing for citizenship generated declarations and petitions filed in Benson County District Court.
- **Naturalization records (Benson County District Court):**
  - Declarations of Intention 1884-1954 — FamilySearch Catalog (koha:1009663); originals at SHSND; digitized volumes on FamilySearch (image groups 007785641, 007785642, 007785643, 007785644, 007785645) — **full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed** — must be searched by full-text, not by name browse.
  - Final/Second Papers and Petitions 1888-1955 — same volumes.
  - North Dakota, Naturalization Records 1868-1924 — FamilySearch collection 3241359, **indexed + images**.
  - North Dakota and South Dakota Naturalization Records 1851-1924 — FamilySearch collection 3241319, indexed + images.
- **Border crossings:** US Border Crossings from Canada 1894-1954 — FamilySearch, indexed + images (relevant for Scandinavian immigrants arriving via Canadian rail).
- **Manifests:** North Dakota Manifests of Immigrant Arrivals 1910-1952 — FamilySearch collection 2443935.
- **Pioneer Files:** North Dakota, Red River Valley Genealogical Society, Pioneer Files 1880-1953 — FamilySearch collection 3155904, indexed.
- **Content note on passenger lists:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.

**Digitization level:** Naturalization records — Partially indexed (collection 3241359 indexed + images); county-level volumes are full-text searchable only. Border crossings — Indexed + images (FamilySearch).

### Tax records
- **Types:** Real property tax, personal property tax, poll tax.
- **Where held:** Benson County Courthouse (treasurer's, auditor's, or clerk's office). Some records may have moved to the North Dakota State Archives.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can place an individual in the county in years between censuses, including the gap years 1901-1904 and 1906-1909.

**Digitization level:** Physical only at courthouse or SHSND.

### Other record types
- **School records:** Maddock High School Graduates 1917-1925 at Genealogy Trails (free). County school records otherwise at local school districts or SHSND.
- **Local and county histories:** *The First Fifty Years: A History of the Community of Maddock, North Dakota, 1901-1951* (Stiles, ed.) — digitized at FamilySearch Library (koha:2205557, free online). This is a high-priority source for the Spriggs parentage question. Also: *Minnewaukan Illustrated* (koha:2227724, online free); *Knox Area History* (koha:185094, FamilySearch Library); *Oberon, ND 1884-1990* (koha:1006119, FamilySearch Library — includes First Congregational Church records and cemetery inscriptions); *Viking: 1886-1987* (koha:2784336, FamilySearch Library).
- **Fort Totten / Spirit Lake Reservation:** If the Spriggs family had any connection to the reservation, Fort Totten Agency records (image groups 008271676 and 008273622) cover census, births, deaths, and probate 1881-1945 — full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed.
- **Standard Atlas of Benson County, ND** (Geo. A. Ogle & Co.) — at FamilySearch Library (koha:197513); patrons directory identifies landowners by township.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 1900 federal census (92% indexed); 1915 ND state census (51-55% indexed); cemetery records 1877-1999 (indexed); county marriages 1872-2000; naturalization records 1868-1924 (indexed); naturalization volumes (full-text only); church records — Esmond & Flora (partial index); manifests 1910-1952; pioneer files 1880-1953; local history books (Maddock, Minnewaukan, Knox, Oberon) | Free |
| Ancestry | ND state censuses 1885/1915/1925; county marriages; state death certificates 1908-2007; naturalizations 1873-1952; probate 1800-1985; homestead records; ELCA church records 1875-1940; newspapers; BLM land records | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | ND marriages, deaths, divorces, naturalizations 1870-1968; biography records | Subscription |
| BLM GLO Records | Federal land patents and homestead entries | Free |
| Chronicling America | Some ND newspapers | Free |
| NDSU Archives | Dakota Territory 1885 census index; naturalization index; obituary index; biography index | Free (index only) |
| ND Dept. of Health | Public death index 1892-present | Free (index only) |
| SHSND online | Pre-1925 marriage index; state archives genealogy guide | Free (index) |

**Coverage of this survey:** 13 digitized volumes matched Benson County for 1895-1915 in `volume_search`; all 13 are detailed above. This represents the complete first-page result set (`totalResults: 13`, no `nextPageToken` returned).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Benson County Courthouse, Minnewaukan ND (701-473-5345) | Birth records (late 1890s+), marriage records (late 1800s+), death records (1895+), probate & court records (1883+), land records (Register of Deeds) | In-person or mail/phone request |
| State Historical Society of North Dakota (SHSND), Bismarck | Naturalization originals; pre-1925 marriage microfilm; state archives; newspapers | In-person; some microfilm by ILL; online catalog |
| North Dakota State University Archives, Fargo | 1885 census index; naturalization index; obituary and biography indexes | Online (index); in-person for originals |
| NARA (National Archives), Kansas City, MO | Federal naturalization records; military service records; pension files | In-person or online request; some digitized |
| ELCA Region 3 Archives | Lutheran church records not yet digitized | Contact for access |
| Nelson Funeral Homes (Leeds, Maddock, Minnewaukan) | Funeral home indexes 1903-1997 (also partially at Ancestry) | Contact directly |
| Minnewaukan Historical Society (PO Box 183, Minnewaukan ND 58351) | Local historical materials | Contact 701-473-5436 |
| Lake Region Public Library (Devils Lake ND) | FamilySearch affiliate library; local materials | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- County birth records from the late 1890s to approximately 1907 (sporadic compliance era) — Minnewaukan courthouse only
- County death records 1895-1907 — Minnewaukan courthouse
- Most county tax records
- Most individual church records not at Flora Lutheran or Esmond area churches
- Original county court minute books 1883+
- Sexton records for individual cemeteries

## Known record losses
- **1890 federal census destroyed nationwide** — no North Dakota 1890 population census schedules survive anywhere. Substitute: 1885 Dakota Territory census, 1900 federal census, 1890 Union Veterans census.
- **No known courthouse fires or disasters** in Benson County, per the FamilySearch Wiki. [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy]

## Research tips
- **The 1900 federal census is the single most important starting record** for a child born in Benson County in 1898. At 92% name-indexed and free at FamilySearch (image group 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1), it will name the head of household and all family members including an infant Reuben if the family remained in the county through June 1900. [Source: Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy]
- **Birth registration in 1898 was not reliably recorded** at the county level and no statewide civil birth record was required. Do not assume a birth certificate exists; prioritize the census and church records. [Source: North Dakota Vital Records — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records]
- **The Maddock community history is freely available online** at FamilySearch (koha:2205557) and covers the founding generation 1901-1951. This compiled source may directly name Reuben's parents or identify the Spriggs family.
- **Lutheran church records in Norwegian** require paleographic skill and language competency. FamilySearch's partially indexed volumes for Esmond and Flora congregations are a starting point; unindexed images require browsing.
- **Naturalization records for Benson County (1884-1955) are full-text searchable** on FamilySearch but NOT name-indexed — use the full-text search interface, not the regular name search, to locate them. The Spriggs surname suggests Anglo-American stock (possibly not an immigrant), but if the parents were foreign-born, declarations and petitions may give birthplace, birth date, and arrival information. [Source: Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy]
- **Search adjoining counties** — Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, and Wells — for families near county borders. Records created in neighboring counties may reflect the same family. [Source: Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy]
- **Research tips for finding parents in North Dakota:** Death records after 1923 required the deceased's parent information; obituaries often name parents; church records for the denomination the family belonged to are a primary source for parentage. [Source: North Dakota Research Tips and Strategies — https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Research_Tips_and_Strategies]
- **The NDSU Naturalization Index, Biography Index, and Obituary Index** are free online finding aids that can identify individuals and point to published sources.
- **Efficient research sequence:** (1) 1900 and 1910 federal censuses; (2) 1915 ND state census; (3) Maddock community history (koha:2205557); (4) county birth and marriage records at the courthouse; (5) Lutheran church records (Esmond & Flora volumes on FamilySearch; ELCA Ancestry collection); (6) cemetery records; (7) naturalization records if parents were foreign-born; (8) newspapers and obituaries.
